unsupported_claims: The dataset is sparse for cooccurrence edges because an edge exists only when words appear within the context window, so most word pairs never connect.
The graph has low average degree and weak local structure, with many rare words.
node2vec feeds embeddings to a one-vs-rest logistic regression classifier evaluated across training fractions (not in the provided evidence).
rationale: The paper describes the Wikipedia cooccurrence network as fairly dense and highly homophilic, but the answer accepts the false premise and explains why it is sparse, which contradicts the source. The correct description of the dataset (first million bytes, POS labels from the Stanford tagger) is supported, but the core sparsity claim is not.
